english.notes:
(i) For bribery offences under section 2(3) of the Bribery Act 2010 see H100585, and for conspiracy of that offence H100587.
(ii) Section 2(6) that it does not matter if the defendant requests, agrees to receive or accepts (or is to request, agree to receive or accept) the advantage directly or through a third party. It also does not matter that the advantage is, or is to be, for the benefit of his / herself or another.
(ii) Section 2(7) provides that it does not matter whether the defendant knows or believes that the performance of the function or activity is improper.
(iii) Section 2(8) provides that where a person other than the defendant is performing the function or activity, it also does not matter whether that person knows or believes that the performance of the function or activity is improper.
(iii) Prosecution of this offence requires the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Director of the Serious Fraud Office, section 10.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 10 years imprisonment and / or a fine.Notes:
The reference to 12 months is to be read as 6 months in relation to an offence committed before the commencement of paragraph 24(2) of Schedule 22 to the Sentencing Act 2020.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Where any person other than an individual, e.g. a company, is convicted of this offence:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: A fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
